entities.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Al-Azhar Mosque (Arabic: الجامع الأزهر, Al-Jāmiʿ al-Azhar — 'The Most Resplendent Mosque') in Cairo, Egypt, founded in 970–972 CE by the Fatimid Caliph al-Muizz's general Jawhar al-Siqilli — is one of the world's oldest mosques and universities, and the most important institution of Sunni Islamic scholarship in the world. Al-Azhar University (founded alongside the mosque) is the world's oldest continuously operating university (predating Bologna by over a century), and Al-Azhar's scholarly opinions (fatwas) on Islamic jurisprudence, theology, and contemporary issues carry authoritative weight throughout the Sunni Muslim world.

Al-Azhar's founding by the Fatimid Caliphate (a Shi'a Ismaili dynasty) as an Ismaili institution is a profound historical irony: after Saladin (Salah ad-Din, founder of the Ayyubid dynasty) overthrew the Fatimids in 1171, Al-Azhar was converted to Sunni Shafi'i use and eventually became the greatest center of Sunni scholarship — despite its Ismaili origins. Al-Azhar's evolution reflects Islamic history's complex sectarian transformations and the remarkable adaptability of religious institutions.

In the modern era, Al-Azhar serves as the most authoritative voice of mainstream Sunni Islam globally: its fatwas on contested issues (suicide bombing, interfaith marriage, Islamic finance) are followed by Muslim communities worldwide, and its certification of Islamic educational materials influences the curriculum in Muslim-majority countries across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. With approximately 500,000 students from 100+ countries, Al-Azhar University remains the world's largest institution of Islamic education.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Al-Azhar Mosque and University — founded 970 CE, the world's most authoritative Sunni Islamic scholarly institution for over 1,000 years, one of the oldest continuously operating universities, shaping Islamic jurisprudence for 1.8 billion Muslims — is among the most historically significant religious and educational institutions in human history.
